SNUGLITE (blind test): telemetry recovered from orbital physics

Every field below was found without a decoder: candidate byte readings were tested against sunlight, thermal lag, orbital phase, wall-clock time and the IGRF magnetic field computed from the TLE. Names, units and scales are Claude's reading of that evidence, with the satellite name withheld.

Frame type raw:len97

1005 frames, 126 passes, 97-byte payload

A 97-byte beacon containing a fast-running u4 counter, a GNSS position and velocity block (ECEF/ECI, about 1e5 raw per km, so units of 10 m), and a smooth narrow-band battery-like value at offset 59. Many GNSS fields hold -1 (no fix) in most frames, which is why the position fields show spurious sun correlations.

Health. No reboots were seen: the counter shows 0 resets in 16 days. The battery-like voltage is stable with no measurable drift, and it dips in shadow and recovers in sun as expected. There is no thermal data, so the evidence is limited.

Frame type raw:len214

405 frames, 108 passes, 214-byte payload

A 214-byte housekeeping/telemetry beacon containing counters, a GNSS fix (ECEF position and velocity, with no-fix values of -1 in most frames), an attitude quaternion, solar-array currents or powers, and a group of temperatures. Temperature-like signed bytes show thermal inertia of about 20 min. The orbit is LEO at 481 km, and every frame has an eclipse in the previous 80 min.

Health. No reboots are visible: the u4 counters have no resets, and the u2 counter that wraps does so by design. Battery voltage (about 8.1-8.3 V) looks charged by sunlight, though its daily low drifts down by about 15 per 30 days; over 16 days this could be seasonal, so I am not sure it is ageing. Temperatures swing normally with the eclipse cycle, so I see no thermal anomaly.
